facts: When assessing the rumen, examiners must look for signs of bloat.
The stages or classifications of bloat listed are mild bloat, moderate bloat, and severe bloat.
Diagram figures 1, 2, and 3 depict the progressive flank distension associated with bloat in cattle.
Displacement of the abomasum is common in dairy cattle.
Under normal anatomy, the rumen is positioned on the left side and the abomasum is positioned ventrally towards the right.
In a cow with an LDA (Left Displaced Abomasum), the abomasum (red) shifts to the left side between the body wall and the rumen (blue).
The normal respiratory rate in adult dairy cattle is 10-30 beats (breaths) per minute.
The normal respiratory rate in calves is 15-40 beats (breaths) per minute.
Clinical signs to look for when evaluating the respiratory system include difficulty in breathing, nasal discharges, and fever and inappetence.
